odc_type: incorrect type inference for prototype inheritance
observation_summary: The compiler incorrectly reports that properties defined on a superclass prototype are missing on a subclass instance when the subclass prototype is defined via an object literal.
reasoning_summary: The bug occurs because the compiler fails to correctly associate the prototype of a constructor with its superclass when the prototype is defined using an object literal. When a constructor extends another, the compiler expects the prototype chain to be correctly established. In the buggy version, the compiler failed to update the implicit prototype of the object literal assigned to the constructor's prototype property, leading to 'Property never defined' warnings because the compiler could not resolve inherited properties. The fix involves explicitly resetting the implicit prototype of the object literal to match the superclass's prototype, ensuring the type system correctly identifies inherited members.
